attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: Firm 'will' / 'will not soon' language makes this a scored forecast. The normalisation keeps both the assisting-tool part and the 'not soon replace' part, plus their scope.

contract.note: The plain reading of 'replace' as broad substitution across the whole developer role matches the surrounding text. The contract rightly declines to invent a deadline for 'soon', and its early-resolution rule is reasonable.

evidence.note: Fed staff preprint dated March 2026: coder employment is still growing, but more slowly. It is consistent with no replacement but does not settle an open-ended forecast.

Anthropic's account of its own company, available Oct 2026, before the cutoff. It shows less hiring and task automation at one firm, with continued human oversight. It is not evidence of widespread replacement.

reviews.rationale: 'Soon' sets no deadline, and the packet has no dated, independently confirmed event of widespread replacement that would meet the early-resolution rule. The employment data and one company's report bear on the question without settling it, so the forecast cannot be scored yet.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: A firm present-tense capability claim about learning APIs. The programming-language extension is hedged ('maybe'), so it is not scored. The normalisation keeps that hedge.

contract.note: The low bar of 'help' fits the speaker's 'can help'. Using 2024 as the observation window is the evaluator's choice, not the speaker's. It is reasonable, but it decides which evidence is eligible.

evidence.note: Self-reports from a pilot that ended Jan 2024 say Copilot helped developers learn new languages. That bears only on the hedged language extension, not on the firm API claim.

2024 preprint reporting perceived learning benefits and more confidence with new libraries. The fieldwork dates are not established, it relies on self-reports, and it does not show API learning directly.
Anthropic study from 2026, outside the 2024 window, and a company disclosure. Lower mastery of the library on average does not refute 'can help' under the contract.

reviews.rationale: The firm API part needs evidence from the 2024 window showing useful help in learning unfamiliar APIs. The packet has only self-reported learning benefits that are mostly about languages (the hedged part), plus a study whose dates are unclear. The 2026 study is outside the window and does not contradict a 'can help' claim. The evidence does not settle the claim.
